key_insight: Co-LMLM extends limited-memory language models by using continuous query keys to retrieve textual knowledge from an external knowledge base during generation. This preserves factual control while making knowledge access more flexible than discrete retrieval schemes.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of storing and using factual knowledge in language models without forcing it into model weights, while still allowing efficient, controllable retrieval at generation time.
method: Pairs continuous-valued keys with text-based knowledge values in an external knowledge base.
Uses the model's query representation to fetch relevant knowledge dynamically during generation.
Retains the LMLM paradigm of externalized knowledge to improve controllability and reduce reliance on parametric memory.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Co-LMLM offers a more controllable way to manage factual knowledge, making it easier to update, audit, and steer model behavior. This is especially useful for applications where knowledge freshness and governance matter.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing model, continuous-query module, and external knowledge base
Side-by-side comparison of parametric memory vs. limited memory vs. Co-LMLM
Icon set for knowledge storage, retrieval, and control
paper_title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
paper_authors: Yair Feldman, Linxi Zhao, Nathan Godey, Dongyoung Go, Yilun Hua
